politics.summary: Australian politics today was dominated by two big themes: the RBA's next interest rate move and what Anthropic's potential Australian expansion could mean for the country's energy grid. No major domestic political drama, but both stories have real implications for investors.

stories.title: Anthropic eyes Australia — and wants a big chunk of its electricity
stories.why_it_matters: Anthropic — the AI company behind the Claude chatbot and a major rival to OpenAI — is reportedly looking at setting up large-scale data centre operations in Australia. The catch: AI data centres are enormous power consumers, and Anthropic is said to have its eyes on a significant slice of Australia's electricity output. This raises real questions about energy grid capacity, electricity prices, and where that power would come from. For investors, it's a signal that AI infrastructure demand is coming to Australia in a big way — potentially good for energy companies and bad for power prices.

stories.title: Could ASX 200 banks shift after the RBA call?
stories.why_it_matters: Market analysts are watching the RBA's (Reserve Bank of Australia's) next interest rate decision closely, with debate about whether the big four banks could see share price moves depending on the outcome. If the RBA cuts rates — meaning it makes borrowing cheaper — bank profit margins on loans can narrow, which can weigh on bank stocks. Your VDHG ETF holds some Australian bank exposure, so this is relevant. No decision date specified in the article, but it's a story to track this week.

ai.summary: AI regulation is the big theme today — Trump has signed a new executive order that could change how US AI companies launch their models, while OpenAI rolled out a new security feature to protect against a specific type of attack on AI systems. Anthropic's Australian ambitions also sit at the intersection of AI and local politics.

stories.title: Trump's new AI order could change how OpenAI, Google, and Anthropic launch models
stories.why_it_matters: President Trump has signed a new executive order aimed at shaping how America's biggest AI companies — OpenAI, Google (your GOOG holding), and Anthropic — release new AI models. The order could introduce requirements or restrictions around model launches, potentially slowing how quickly these companies can bring new products to market. That's a headwind worth watching for GOOG and your GXAI ETF, which holds many of these same companies. The details of the order are still being digested by the industry.

stories.title: OpenAI launches Lockdown Mode to block prompt injection attacks
stories.why_it_matters: OpenAI has released a new 'Lockdown Mode' for its AI systems — essentially a security setting that blocks a type of hack called a 'prompt injection attack'. These attacks work by sneaking malicious instructions into data that an AI reads (like a webpage or document), tricking it into doing something unintended — for example, leaking your private info or ignoring your instructions. Lockdown Mode prevents the AI from acting on those hidden commands. It's a practical security improvement for businesses using ChatGPT in their workflows.

stories.title: Anthropic eyes Australia and a large slice of its electricity output
stories.why_it_matters: Anthropic is eyeing Australia for major data centre infrastructure, and the scale being discussed could consume a meaningful portion of the country's electricity output. AI data centres require massive, continuous power — think hundreds of megawatts running 24/7. This is part of a global race by AI companies to secure compute capacity outside the US. For Australian investors, it signals growing AI infrastructure investment onshore, with potential flow-on effects for energy stocks and the broader tech sector.

sport.summary: Big weekend in the NRL with some wild scorelines — the Panthers demolished the Tigers 68-0 in one of the most lopsided results you'll ever see, the Dolphins continued their red-hot form, and the Titans upset the Broncos at Suncorp. In the AFL, the Big Freeze at the G went ahead for the first time since Neale Daniher's passing. Kyrgios is back on the tennis court too.

stories.title: Panthers thrash Tigers 68-0 — Nathan Cleary fires State of Origin warning
stories.why_it_matters: Panthers put on a clinic against the Tigers on Sunday, winning 68-0 at CommBank Stadium — yes, 68-nil. Nathan Cleary was in devastating form and reportedly used the match to send a warning to State of Origin selectors. The Tigers were booed off by their own fans, and Nine described the result as 'almost cruel'. One of the biggest winning margins in NRL history.

stories.title: Dolphins thrash Cowboys 40-14, Origin stars shine in fifth-straight win
stories.why_it_matters: The Dolphins are flying — five wins in a row after dismantling the Cowboys 40-14 in Townsville on Saturday. Origin stars were in top form for the Phins. The Cowboys also copped bad news with a North Queensland gun facing suspension after a third high-tackle offence — Fox Sports reports he's learned his fate from the match review committee.

stories.title: Titans upset Broncos 28-23 at Suncorp — Gold Coast derbies always deliver
stories.why_it_matters: The Gold Coast Titans beat the Brisbane Broncos 28-23 at Suncorp Stadium on Saturday night — a big scalp for the Titans and a real dent to the Broncos' season momentum. Queensland derby games at Suncorp rarely disappoint, and this one delivered.

stories.title: Big Freeze goes ahead for first time since Neale Daniher's death
stories.why_it_matters: The AFL's annual Big Freeze fundraiser at the MCG went ahead on Monday — the first one since the death of Neale Daniher, the former Melbourne coach who became the face of the event and its fight against Motor Neurone Disease (MND). Celebrities slid down the ramp into an ice bath, continuing the tradition Daniher started. A genuinely emotional day for footy fans.

stories.title: Kyrgios confirms latest tennis comeback ahead of Wimbledon
stories.why_it_matters: Nick Kyrgios has confirmed another comeback to professional tennis with Wimbledon on the horizon. No details on which tournament he'll play first, but the announcement confirms he's targeting the grass court season. Kyrgios has had multiple injury-interrupted comebacks in recent years — whether this one sticks remains to be seen.
